author: Teresa Elena Frontado,Han Li,Zhang Tong
description:
Polls began closing across the United States on Tuesday evening in midterm elections that will decide whether US President Donald Trump’s Republicans keep control of Congress, after a day of voting disrupted by floods and machine glitches but largely free of the problems many had feared.
The first polls closed at 6pm Eastern Time (7am Hong Kong time), with most states following over the next several hours. The last state to close polls will be Alaska, at 1am Eastern Time (2pm Hong Kong time)....
title: US midterms: what happened while Asia slept, and when to expect results

author: Liu Zhen
description:
Amid continuously escalating tensions, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi on Tuesday accused a handful of Philippine politicians of “egregious, irrational and intolerable” conduct, urging Manila to rein in their anti-China rhetoric, state media reported.
Wang made the remarks during a phone conversation with Philippine Foreign Minister Theresa Lazaro, as China-Philippines relations were currently facing what he described as “malicious interference”, according to Xinhua.
“Some Philippine...
title: China accuses Philippine politicians of ‘intolerable’ conduct as tensions rise

author: Khushboo Razdan
description:
Last week, Somaliland, a breakaway region that declared independence from Somalia in 1991, welcomed its first ambassador from Israel.
Diplomat Michael Lotem presented his credentials in Hargeisa, while officials laid the cornerstone for an Israeli embassy. The ceremony, announced by Israel’s foreign ministry on Sunday, formalised a relationship that began with mutual recognition in December.
Somalia, the African Union, Arab states and China strongly oppose the move, reaffirming Somaliland as...
title: Israel deepens Somaliland ties with first ambassador, testing Horn of Africa balance

author: Liu Zhen
description:
Zhang Shengmin, China’s most senior uniformed general, met Russian Defence Minister Andrey Belousov in Beijing on Tuesday in his first publicly reported meeting with a foreign official since he became a member of the Politburo.
Zhang, the vice-chairman of China’s Central Military Commission (CMC), pledged to deepen military cooperation and strategic coordination with Russia during the meeting at the Diaoyutai State Guesthouse.
He was elected to the Politburo last week at a key Communist Party...
title: Top Chinese general meets Russian defence minister days after Politburo appointment

author: Phoebe Zhang
description:
A Chinese court has begun hearings in a defamation case filed by authorities and institutes in Beijing and Wuhan against the US state of Missouri over accusations tied to Covid-19.
In a notice on Monday, the Wuhan Intermediate People’s Court said it held a hearing on Friday and legal proceedings were continuing.
The case was jointly filed on April 30, 2025 by the Wuhan government in Hubei province, the Chinese Academy of Sciences and its subordinate entity, the Wuhan Institute of Virology (WIV),...
title: Chinese court hears US$53.5 billion Covid defamation case against US state of Missouri

author: Liu Zhen
description:
China appears to be testing a stealthy new trimaran at sea, according to a photograph circulating on social media, in what could be a further effort to develop unconventional naval platforms.
The image first emerged on Weibo on Sunday and appears to show a vessel featuring an inverted wave-piercing bow, three-hull design and angular superstructure surfaces that could be intended to reduce its radar signature.
The vessel, which is fitted with a prominent antenna mast and multiple dome-shaped...
title: China tests wave-piercing stealth trimaran as unconventional naval fleet grows

author: Orange Wang
description:
China has pledged to work with Pakistan to advance “high-level security cooperation” and ensure the two countries’ flagship infrastructure project is “safe”, as terrorism continues to disrupt a key region for the Belt and Road Initiative.
Liu Haixing, head of the party’s International Department, sent the messages during separate meetings with Pakistan’s top military leader Asim Munir and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Monday, as part of his first official visit to the South Asian country...
title: Beijing offers to boost China-Pakistan corridor safety as terror threat grows

author: Albee Zhang
description:
A People’s Liberation Army air defence unit has for the first time intercepted two new types of missile simultaneously during a drill – including one that made a sudden change of direction, according to state television.
The CCTV report on Monday said it was a rapid response operation by the ground-based Shenwei Missile Battalion – under the PLA Central Theatre Command Air Force – which is equipped with Hongqing surface-to-air missiles.
It did not disclose the type of missiles intercepted or any...
title: China’s HQ series intercepts 2 new missile types as PLA tests weapon platform

author: Cao Jiaxuan
description:
China’s embassy in Papua New Guinea has disputed reports that a suspected Chinese-made artillery shell was found in a shipping container in Port Moresby, saying the object was instead a shell-shaped wine bottle.
The embassy said in a social media post on Tuesday it was awaiting the official findings of an investigation by the Royal Papua New Guinea Constabulary (RPNGC).
It cited an on-site verification by a company involved in the case, which said the object was a wine bottle. “It poses no...
title: What is it? PNG says it’s an artillery shell. China says it’s a wine bottle

author: SCMP
description:
This article was first published on November 4, 2011.
China a step closer to building its own space station
by Stephen Chen
Encouraged by yesterday (November 3, 2011) morning’s historic rendezvous and docking of the Shenzhou VIII spacecraft, Chinese authorities said construction of a space station will begin as soon as 2013.
“We will do two more rendezvous and docking flights next year,” said Wu Ping (武平), spokeswoman for the manned space programme, at a press conference in Beijing yesterday....
title: China’s historic first space docking in 2011 – SCMP archive

author: Shi Huang
description:
An anticancer drug developed by Sichuan Biokin Pharmaceutical took centre stage in a late-breaking oral presentation at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress in Madrid last week.
Researchers said the drug, iza-bren, showed a significant advantage over platinum-based chemotherapy in a phase 3 randomised, double-blind clinical trial conducted at 73 hospitals in China and involving 432 patients with advanced lung cancer.
The median progression-free survival (PFS) – the length of...
title: Chinese drug iza-bren doubles lung cancer survival window in phase 3 trial

author: Fan Chen
description:
The United States has attacked an Iranian island in the Strait of Hormuz, the latest in a series of covert, limited strikes ahead of the US midterm elections, as President Donald Trump signalled progress in talks with Tehran.
Iran’s Qeshm Island was struck on Monday, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing US officials, some of whom framed the strikes as defensive and aimed at deterring Tehran’s attacks on commercial ships in the critical chokepoint.
Iranian media reported that five blasts were...
title: US strikes Iran’s Qeshm Island ahead of midterms as Trump says deal ‘could happen’

author: Junjie Wang
description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping met four foreign leaders in October – two each from Africa and Europe – with the month dominated by the Communist Party Central Committee’s fifth plenum.
The pace will probably pick up in November. Xi has already met Oman’s Sultan Haitham bin Tariq, and he will host an Apec summit on November 18–19. The Shenzhen event will probably feature talks with US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and other regional leaders.
title: Xi Jinping meets foreign leaders: tracker, October 2026

author: Alcott Wei
description:
A key document endorsed by the Communist Party proposed stronger oversight of principal leaders below the central level, barring them from demanding personal allegiance from their leadership teams – a demand that is only for the top leaders.
The proposal is part of a 17,000-word resolution approved at the fifth plenum of the 20th Central Committee, the full text of which was published by state news agency Xinhua on Sunday.
The four-day plenum last week emphasised internal governance, discipline...
title: ‘Speak last’: China’s fifth plenum moves to rein in party leaders

author: Josephine Ma
description:
China’s ruling Communist Party has pledged to target “old nice persons” within its ranks as it steps up its anti-corruption drive ahead of a major leadership reshuffle next year.
Rendered in Chinese as lao hao ren, the term refers to unprincipled, conflict-averse officials who turn a blind eye to misconduct to protect their own careers and social standing.
A resolution adopted at the close of the party’s 20th Central Committee’s fifth plenum last week signalled a crackdown on this culture of...
title: China’s Communist Party plenum targets passive ‘nice’ guys in anti-corruption push

author: Nayan Seth,Lucy Quaggin
description:
A top OpenAI executive said on Monday that Washington needs to be “clear-eyed” and “aware” about sharing information with Beijing during coming talks on artificial intelligence (AI), while also warning about the threat posed by alleged Chinese distillation attacks.
“Be very clear-eyed. Be very aware of what information you are able to expect in return for what you are sharing, and start to build a foundation,” said Caroline Zier, OpenAI’s deputy lead for national security, during a discussion at...
title: OpenAI executive urges caution in China-US AI talks, warns of distillation threats

author: Teresa Elena Frontado
description:
Americans go to the polls on Tuesday, November 3, in midterm elections that could reshape the final two years of Donald Trump’s second term as president.
Control of both chambers of Congress is in play, along with 36 governorships. Polls suggest Democrats go into the vote with an advantage, but the outcome will hinge on a few dozen closely fought races.
More than 100 million people are expected to vote if turnout matches the 2022 midterms. By October 12, a record US$3.8 billion had been spent on...
title: US midterm elections 2026: all you need to know
